newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's Alarcon evaluates cabinet shuffle.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Alarcon evaluates cabinet shuffle.

text.p: Ecuador's President Fabian Alarcon is set to shuffle his cabinet next week after the approval of his government in Sunday's referendum, a government source said on Monday.
The source told Reuters the president had not decided on the makeup of his new cabinet but the changes will be announced "after next Monday."

An exit poll and a projection based on early returns by two seperate firms showed 74 percent of Ecuadoreans endorsed on Sunday the removal of former President Abdala Bucaram after Congress declared him "mentally unfit" six months after taking office.
Three seperate polling companies also showed that between 62 and 65 percent of voters endorsed Alarcon as interim president until new elections next May.

According to the source, Administration Secretary Arturo Gangotena, Government Minister Cesar Verduga, Education Minister Mario Jaramillo and Agriculture Minister Alfredo Saltos offered to resign for the president to nominate new ministers.
The source said other ministers offered to stand down as well. "The president has the legitimate right to reorganize the cabinet," Gangotena told journalists.
He said the resignations were in line with the objective of making political changes that Ecuador needs, after the government's legitimacy was underlined at the polls.
